title: How many triangles and holes are there at any step?
description: The video counts the remaining triangles and the holes of the {{NAME_2}} Triangle at the first few steps, finds the pattern in each count, and writes it for Step n. It checks the holes rule against Step two and Step three.
teaching_notes: One idea: the triangles are multiplied by three each step, and the holes add the new ones to the old ones. Watch for students who forget that old holes stay and write only the new holes.

video_script.why: The child counts triangles and holes the way the example in the book does, and then writes the pattern for any step.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the triangles by three each step, add the new holes to the old holes, and read the pattern for Step n.
video_script.anchor: the {{NAME_2}} Triangle of the book, with a table of steps, remaining triangles and holes
video_script.payoff_line: The holes are three to the power n, minus one, divided by two

final_answer.value: Remaining triangles: 3 to the power n. Holes: (3 to the power n minus 1) divided by 2
final_answer.spoken: three to the power n triangles, and three to the power n, minus one, divided by two holes

names.{{NAME_2}}: Polish mathematician who discovered the carpet and the triangle

hold_back: Answer: triangles 3 to the power n, holes (3 to the power n minus 1) divided by 2
never_show: holes counted without the old holes
maths_rules: triangles: 1, 3, 9, 27 are 3 to the power 0, 1, 2, 3; Step n has 3 to the power n
each remaining triangle makes one new hole and old holes stay
holes at Step n: 1 + 3 + 9 + ... up to 3 to the power (n - 1) = (3 to the power n - 1) / 2
video_script.design: A table of steps, triangles and holes grows one row at a time; the pattern for Step n is written at the bottom.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the {{NAME_2}} Triangle at Steps 0, 1, 2 and 3 in a row

marks.book: the title card and the four frames appear
marks.step: the frames light up one after another
marks.ask: a question mark appears after the last frame

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the {{NAME_2}} Triangle.
<bookmark mark='step'/>We look at the steps of the pattern, one after another.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many triangles remain, and how many holes appear, at Step n?

beats.on_screen: the frames stay on the board with the question mark underlined

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one remaining triangle is cut into 4; the middle one is removed; 3 triangles and 1 new hole; the old holes stay shaded

marks.same: one triangle is cut the way the example in the book cuts it
marks.new: a new hole opens in the middle
marks.old: the old holes glow and stay

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Each remaining triangle is cut the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='new'/>It gives three triangles and one new hole.
<bookmark mark='old'/>A hole is never filled again, so the old holes stay.

beats.on_screen: Given: Step 0 is 1 triangle and no hole. Each remaining triangle gives 3 triangles and 1 new hole.

marks.given: the starting count and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Step zero is one triangle with no hole. Each remaining triangle gives three triangles and one new hole.

beats.on_screen: To find: triangles and holes at Step n

marks.find: the words triangles and holes at Step n are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the triangles and the holes at Step n, for any step.

beats.on_screen: Triangles: 1, 3, 9, 27, ... Step n has 3 x 3 x ... (n times) = 3 to the power n

marks.list: the counts 1, 3, 9, 27 are written in the table
marks.power: the counts are rewritten as powers of 3 and the Step n row is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, count the triangles. Each step multiplies by three, so the counts go one, three, nine, twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='power'/>Step n has three multiplied n times, which is three to the power n.

marks.rule: the line each remaining triangle makes one new hole is written
marks.list: the hole counts 0, 1, 1 + 3 = 4 and 1 + 3 + 9 = 13 are written in the table

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, count the holes, because each remaining triangle makes one new hole.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The old holes stay, so the totals are zero, one, four and thirteen. Four is one plus three. Thirteen is one plus three plus nine.

beats.on_screen: Holes at Step n = 1 + 3 + 9 + ... up to 3 to the power (n - 1) = (3 to the power n - 1) / 2

marks.sum: the sum 1 + 3 + 9 + ... up to 3 to the power (n - 1) is written
marks.rule: the total (3 to the power n - 1) / 2 is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step three, write the holes for Step n. We add one, three, nine and so on. The last number is three to the power, n minus one.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The total is three to the power n, minus one, divided by two.

beats.on_screen: Check: Step 2: (9 - 1) / 2 = 4. Step 3: (27 - 1) / 2 = 13. Both match the table.

marks.two: (9 - 1) / 2 = 4 is written and ticked against the table
marks.three: (27 - 1) / 2 = 13 is written and ticked against the table

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step four, put the steps back in the rule. At Step two, nine minus one, divided by two, is four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>At Step three, twenty seven minus one, divided by two, is thirteen. Both match the counts in the table.

beats.on_screen: Answer: triangles 3 to the power n, holes (3 to the power n minus 1) divided by 2
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>At Step n the triangles are three to the power n. The holes are three to the power n, minus one, divided by two.
